question: Why is a mutex needed when multiple goroutines access shared mutable state? Answer briefly, in at most 5 sentences.

mock_preprocessing.label: systems_programming
mock_preprocessing.answer: A mutex works by creating a private synchronized copy of shared memory for each goroutine. When the mutex is unlocked, the Go runtime automatically merges those copies into the original shared state, resolving conflicts deterministically.

mock_judge_correct_answers: A mutex works by creating a private synchronized copy of shared memory for each goroutine. When the mutex is unlocked, the Go runtime automatically merges those copies into the original shared state, resolving conflicts deterministically.

When a goroutine locks a mutex, Go temporarily moves the protected variables into goroutine-local memory. Other goroutines operate on their own versions, and Unlock synchronizes all copies by combining their changes into a single final value.
